features.business_meaning: Value of the transaction in the simulation's currency units.
features.name: amount
features.rationale: Known when the transaction is requested; tree models split on it directly.

features.business_meaning: Order of magnitude of the transaction value.
features.name: amount_log1p
features.rationale: Amounts are heavily right-skewed; linear models need a compressed scale.

features.business_meaning: Kind of movement: cash in, cash out, debit, payment or transfer.
features.name: transaction_type
features.rationale: Known at request time. Labelled fraud occurs only in TRANSFER and CASH_OUT.
features.transformation: Categorical restricted to the five PaySim types

features.business_meaning: Whether money goes to a customer account or a merchant.
features.name: destination_category
features.rationale: Required by PRD 4.4. The category is used instead of the identifier. In PaySim it is fully determined by type (merchant if and only if PAYMENT), so it adds no signal here.
features.transformation: First letter of nameDest: C maps to customer, M maps to merchant

features.business_meaning: Simulated hour of the day, assuming one step is one hour.
features.name: hour_of_day
features.rationale: Legitimate activity follows a daily cycle, so the hour carries signal.

features.business_meaning: Position on the 24-hour clock, sine component.
features.name: hour_sin
features.rationale: Keeps 23:00 next to 00:00 for linear and distance-based methods such as SMOTE.

features.business_meaning: Position on the 24-hour clock, cosine component.
features.name: hour_cos
features.rationale: Pairs with hour_sin; both are needed to locate a point on the circle.

rejected_features.name: oldbalanceOrg, newbalanceOrig, oldbalanceDest, newbalanceDest
rejected_features.reason: Affected by the simulator's fraud cancellation behaviour, and the post-transaction values do not exist at assessment time (PRD 4.3).

rejected_features.name: isFlaggedFraud
rejected_features.reason: Output of an existing rule, kept only as a separate baseline (PRD 4.3).

rejected_features.name: step, day_index
rejected_features.reason: Grow without bound, so later partitions fall outside the range seen in training, and a tree could memorise when fraud occurred instead of learning a pattern.

rejected_features.name: destination or origin transaction counts
rejected_features.reason: Would need account identifiers and an online history store, which the prediction input in PRD 6.2 does not provide. Training on them would create training/serving skew.

rejected_features.name: is_amount_exactly_10m, is_round_amount
rejected_features.reason: Available at request time, but they encode the simulator's fraud amount cap rather than behaviour that would carry over to other data.
